credited_works: Georgius Pachymeres, Paraphrasis in omnia opera Dionysii Areopagitae (NEW, 71-568, interwoven)
conclusive_evidence_this_pass: data/pd_research/cgpg_split_proposals.json PG003: every work range interleaves Pseudo-Dionysius' text with Georgius Pachymeres' paraphrase chapter by chapter, plus embedded quotations (e.g. Gregory of Nazianzus' hymn at locus 310); word counts of the ranges are roughly double the TLG word counts for this reason.

The proposals' consistency review: the Pachymeres entry (71-568) fully overlaps all five Dionysius works and is self-flagged 'interwoven, not separable by column range; a splitter must treat it as an annotation, not a carve'.

The five Dionysius column ranges themselves verify (boundaries pinned by verbatim explicit+incipit pairs at 192/193, 299/300, 505/506, 539/540), but carving them would serve each Dionysius work with the Pachymeres paraphrase silently embedded, roughly doubling every work and mis-attributing the paraphrase text.
why_not_resolved:
The record has now been wrong twice, in opposite directions, and this is the second correction. The original said the two authors interleave passage by passage and that no display titles survive in the OCR. The first half was right and the second was not: 26 heads do survive, garbled where Migne printed Latin, and finding them prompted a correction on 2026-08-07 claiming the interleave was block scale and a locus carve could express it. That claim came from a detector reading only the first four words of each row, which could not have found a mid-row head if one existed. Scanning whole rows, 15 of 26 heads fall mid-row, including 1 of the 5 author switches (SYNOPSIS CAPITIS at locus 481, character 1,713 of a 2,018-character row). So the original reason stands: this needs passage-level segmentation inside the row, which carve_cgpg_volume.py cannot express because it moves whole rows. The heads the OCR dropped still need the page images as well.

Checked 2026-08-07 and NOT a further blocker: the printed volume also carries Corderius' annotations and an apparatus criticus, which would each be a separate disposition, but neither is in our served text. Our OCR captured the Greek columns only. What blocks the carve is still the two things above, the dropped heads and the mid-row boundaries.
recommendation: do NOT carve this on loci. A whole-row carve cuts mid-block at every boundary that falls inside a row, and at least one author switch does. Segmenting inside the row needs both a re-OCR that keeps the dropped heads and a splitter that can divide a row, neither of which exists here yet.
precedent: same flag pattern as data/corpus_changes/aelius_dionysius_schwabe.reocr-flag.json (interleaved series a range carve cannot separate)

superseded.was: A column-range carve cannot separate the two authors: each served row alternates Dionysius text and Pachymeres paraphrase at the passage level. Serving the ranges as the Dionysius works would embed a second author's text under the wrong urn; serving the whole volume as Pachymeres would mis-attribute Dionysius. The separation needs passage-level (intra-row) segmentation.
superseded.wrong_because: the bytes do not show a passage-level alternation, and the display heads reported absent are present, garbled. Migne marks each switch with a printed head; the OCR read the Latin ones as Greek letter shapes (PARAPHRASIS PACHYMERAE -> ΡΑΗΑΡΗΚΑΘ ΡΑΩΙΥΜΕΛ at locus 151), which is why a Greek search found none and the interleave was taken to be unmarked.

superseded.was: Not a passage-level problem and not impossible by column carve. Migne prints a display head at every switch, and 4 of them survive in our OCR (plus 7 chapter heads) (measured by scripts/measure_pg003_blocks.py, listed in data/pg003_blocks.json). Every one of them OPENS its row rather than sitting mid-row, so the switches fall on locus boundaries and a locus carve can express them; intra-row segmentation is not what this needs. What blocks the carve is coverage, not granularity: most of the volume's 459 rows sit inside a run whose opening head the OCR dropped, and a boundary we cannot see is exactly the one that would file a block under the wrong author. Recovering the dropped heads needs the PG 3 page images.
superseded.wrong_because: this script measured it with a detector that read only the first four words of each row, so it could only find heads that opened a row, and the conclusion drawn from that ('every switch opens its row, so a locus carve can express them') was circular. Scanning whole rows, 15 of 26 heads fall mid-row.

superseded.was: the record and the issue both describe this as a two-way problem, Dionysius against Pachymeres' paraphrase
superseded.wrong_because: the printed volume holds more than two classes. Its own OCR at the Internet Archive (item Patrologia_Graeca_vol_003) carries the running heads ADNOTATIONES CORDERII 27 times and VARIAE LECTIONES about 138, besides SYNOPSIS CAPITIS and PROLEGOMENA. Corderius' annotations and the apparatus criticus are 19th-century editorial matter, not ancient text.
superseded.but_not_our_problem: none of it is in what we serve. scripts/scan_display_heads.py over cogPG.PG003 returns 48 distinct all-caps words in the whole file and not one is CORDERII, VARIAE, LECTIONES or PROLEGOMENA in any garbling, and no row carries more Latin letters than Greek tokens. The calfa-co OCR took the Greek columns only. So the 160,260 tokens really are Dionysius plus Pachymeres plus a few Greek section heads, and the disposition question of where Corderius' notes and the variae lectiones should go does not arise for this corpus.
